context.body: Another returning traveler encounters a dangerous divine figure near a journey threshold and continues bodily marked.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Jacob crosses his family and possessions, remains alone, and wrestles with an unnamed man through the night.
observations.label: Jacob is interrupted on a return journey: action

observations.body: He receives a wound, a new name, and a blessing, names the place Peniel, and continues alive past the encounter.
observations.label: Jacob is interrupted on a return journey: response

observations.body: return journey · met alone · wrestled · touched · blessed · saw God · life preserved
observations.label: Words in Genesis 32:22–31

payload.posture: Read Genesis 32:22–31 as another dangerous return journey evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The shared narrative shape is real, but Genesis does not mention circumcision, a bridegroom, Moses’ commission, or the firstborn warning.
payload.title: Jacob is interrupted on a return journey
